title: Remove AskResponse.thin_content, merge into content_md
description: thin_content and content_md carry identical content (fr.content_md verbatim) under two field names -- every path that populates thin_content also attaches an explanatory hint (content_thin/content_empty/extraction_empty/llm_error), so the field-name split only encodes 'did I ask or was it forced', a bit the caller already holds (their own include_content param). Remove thin_content entirely; when the forced-attach conditions fire and include_content=False, populate content_md directly. Envelope shape change -- Ask First was raised and the user explicitly confirmed removal (not deprecation) 2026-08-07 during an /opsx:explore session. Also reverts the just-shipped a2web-7bj.3 body_field/retarget_body_field_hints machinery, which becomes dead weight once there's only one field.
close_reason: Removed AskResponse.thin_content entirely. Forced-attach cases (thin_unverified/empty_unverified/corroborated-empty/ask_unanswered) now populate content_md directly instead of a second field -- every case already carries its own explanatory hint (content_thin/content_empty/extraction_empty/llm_error), so a separate field name was pure redundancy on top of information the caller already has. Reverted the a2web-7bj.3 body_field/retarget_body_field_hints machinery (dead weight with one field). Updated ask-response and retrieval-completeness spec Requirements, rewrote 5 tests touching the old field, mutation-verified. make check: 1759 passed, 91.94% coverage, 177 architecture tests.

title: Detect query-term vs served-title mismatch on listings (softer identity check)
description: Split from a2web-axb — the host/title/canonical cross-domain check shipped in commit (fix: served_url_differs hint + confidence cap in build_response, src/a2web/fetcher_response.py). This is the remaining, harder half of that ticket's 'minimum viable check': shapes (b) and (c) from docs/findings/2026-08-07-a2web-call-trace-audit.md §4a2/§4b — same-domain, same-URL-family mismatches where the SERVED content is real and on the right site, but is the wrong product/entity relative to the caller's query (hepsiburada 'pindstrup' search -> shade cloth results; Lenovo 15AKP10 (AMD) asked -> 15IRX10 (Intel) review served). Unlike the host-mismatch check, there is no deterministic URL-level signal here — it needs query-term overlap between the caller's ask/query and the served title/entity, which is fuzzier (tokenization, stemming/locale handling for Turkish/Russian terms in the corpus, threshold tuning against false positives on legitimate paraphrase). Needs its own design pass before implementation, not a quick follow-on to the host check.

title: Detect requested-identity vs served-content mismatch instead of answering high-confidence about the wrong page
description: Audit (docs/findings/2026-08-07-a2web-call-trace-audit.md) §4a/§4a2/§4b. Three observed shapes, all reported at confidence=high: (a) redirect/content swap — a hepsiburada drill URL returned sikayetvar.com 'Decathlon Sikayet' content about bike assembly; a trendyol request returned a hepsiburada title; (b) marketplace search returns a different product family — hepsiburada 'pindstrup' -> shade cloth, 'kekkila' -> Plagron; kaspi 'AMT M-1' -> 387k results in computer/auto parts; batch_15 burned 7 calls on Turkish seedling-tray terms returning baby bath tubs; (c) confusable model variants — asked Lenovo 15AKP10 (AMD), got 15IRX10 (Intel) review; asked ASUS FA607, got FA608WV. Minimum viable check: compare served host/title/canonical against the requested URL, and query-term overlap against returned titles; on mismatch stop asserting high confidence.
close_reason: Shipped the host/registrable-domain half of the 'minimum viable check' (§4a, the worst shape — cross-domain content swaps). build_response now compares registrable_domain(requested_url) vs registrable_domain(final_url); on mismatch it caps a computed 'high' confidence to 'medium' (downgrade-only) and appends a new served_url_differs operator hint naming both URLs. Covers the hepsiburada->sikayetvar and trendyol-title cases in the audit exactly. Test: tests/capabilities/retrieval_completeness/test_served_url_identity_mismatch.py (3 tests, mutation-verified). Spec: openspec/specs/fetch-response/spec.md, new Requirement 'a cross-domain landing caps confidence and is flagged'. The remaining two shapes (§4a2 same-domain wrong-product-family, §4b confusable model variants) need query-term-overlap against served titles, a fuzzier heuristic requiring its own design pass — split off to a2web-byy.

title: Never report confidence on an empty answer; return fetched body when extraction is empty
description: Audit (docs/findings/2026-08-07-a2web-call-trace-audit.md) §4c: 42 calls return status=failed AND confidence=high AND answer="". 35 carry operator_hints extraction_empty — 'Fetched N characters but extraction produced an EMPTY answer', median N=8788, max 78623. Two defects: (1) confidence is asserted over a non-existent answer, making the field unreadable for a caller branching on it; (2) a successfully fetched body of up to 76KB is discarded because one LLM extraction returned empty, leaving the caller nothing. Verified deterministically over the corpus, not model-judged.
close_reason: Fixed. FetchResponse carries a new internal ask_unanswered:bool (exclude=True from wire), set in build_response from the existing ask_unanswered local. build_ask_response reads it to (1) cap confidence to low unconditionally -- the existing obstacle-based cap never fires for a provider error or unconfigured backend, since routing/obstacle is None in both -- and (2) attach the fetched body as thin_content when include_content=False, same fallback channel empty_confirmed already uses. Mutation-verified both directions. openspec/specs/ask-response/spec.md updated with two new scenarios. tests/capabilities/ask_response/test_ask_unanswered_confidence_and_body.py.

title: Listing pages: return per-row structured data, not prose about the table
description: Call-trace audit (docs/findings/2026-08-07-a2web-call-trace-audit.md) over 2856 real calls: 242 listing-page fetches were followed by 885 same-host product-page drilldowns — 31% of the entire corpus. The listing DOM carries price/rating/stock/url per row; query returns prose or an aggregate, so the caller re-derives the table one fetch at a time. a2web already emits listing_partial (95) and listing_more (36), so listing detection exists; the rows do not. Relay every row the page states in its own order — no ranking/filtering (ADR-0012). Envelope shape change: needs Ask First sign-off.

title: content_thin hint names a field the wire does not ship (thin_content)
description:
The content_thin operator hint says 'attached as `thin_content` -- read it to decide which' and 'Read the attached `thin_content`'. There is no thin_content field in the envelope; the body is in content_md. The hint instructs an agent caller to read a field that does not exist.

Dangling-field-name class of bug -- same family as the ~95%% typo that the goldens froze perfectly, and the same lesson: a golden proves a surface has not changed, not that it was right when captured.
acceptance_criteria: The hint names content_md (or whatever field actually carries the body). A test asserts every field name referenced inside an OperatorHint message/fix exists on the envelope that ships it -- otherwise this recurs.
close_reason: Confirmed live on main (not just the deployed build): content_thin/content_empty hints unconditionally named thin_content, which FetchResponse (fetch_raw) never carries and AskResponse only carries when include_content=False. Fixed by parameterizing content_thin_hint/content_empty_hint with body_field (default content_md, correct for FetchResponse and for AskResponse with include_content=True), and adding hints.retarget_body_field_hints, called from build_ask_response once it's known whether the body actually rides thin_content. 3 regression tests (mutation-verified) plus a new ask-response spec Requirement.

title: ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR misclassified as browser_internal_error (blames Playwright, skips try_user_browser)
description:
On the DHL tracking URL, the browser rung produced net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR and a2web emitted:

  code: browser_internal_error
  fix:  'transient browser-driver error -- retry; if it persists the driver (Playwright/Firefox) is at fault, not the target.'

That is almost certainly wrong. An HTTP/2 RST on a DHL tracking endpoint reads as proxy error or edge/WAF bot protection, not a driver bug. This should route to the ADR-0009 try_user_browser critical branch, not to a 'retry, blame Playwright' hint -- misclassifying a wall as a driver defect sends the caller down a dead end and understates severity.

Owner surface: RenderOutcome -> Verdict/OperatorHint mapping in src/a2web/tiers/browser.py.
acceptance_criteria: ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR (and siblings in the same family) map to a wall-shaped verdict with the critical try_user_browser hint; the browser_internal_error mapping is narrowed to errors that really are driver-internal, and both branches are pinned by a test.
close_reason: Fixed in src/a2web/tiers/browser.py: RenderOutcome.error now checks page.detail against a curated set of net-error codes that read as an edge/WAF-level RST or refusal (ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR, ERR_HTTP2_SERVER_REFUSED_STREAM, ERR_QUIC_PROTOCOL_ERROR, ERR_CONNECTION_RESET, ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED, ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED, ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE) -- those get the critical try_user_browser hint instead of browser_internal_error. Everything else (generic driver failures) stays on the narrowed browser_internal_error path, pinned by a dedicated test. Verdict stays connection_error in both cases (only the hint changes). Added openspec Requirement + 2 mutation-verified tests. make check: 1762 passed, 91.93% coverage, 177 architecture tests.

title: SSRF egress denylist for internal/private targets
description:
A networked MCP server fetches any URL a caller supplies from inside its own network -- no egress guard lets a caller pivot into docker service names, tailnet IPs, or cloud metadata. Needs a denylist on the RESOLVED IP (guard DNS-rebind), on redirects, across every tier, with a settings allowlist escape hatch. Revisit before any multi-user or shared-URL exposure.

Full original entry: docs/findings/2026-08-05-backlog-md-archive.md
notes: Threat model: a2web is access-gated, not publicly reachable. Anyone with access to call it already has broader access than an SSRF pivot would grant, so the confused-deputy scenario (caller reaching internal/cloud-metadata targets a2web's network can see but the caller's own network can't) isn't the realistic risk today. Revisit if/when a2web becomes multi-tenant or reachable from a network with a wider access boundary than its callers have. Design notes from the explore session if this is picked back up: infra-level egress firewall (block RFC1918 + 169.254.0.0/16 + 127.0.0.0/8 + 100.64.0.0/10 on the container's OUTPUT chain) is the real enforcement layer and covers raw/browser/site_handler uniformly regardless of tier code path, sidestepping the DNS-rebind check-time/connect-time race entirely; zyte/firecrawl/jina/archive are vendor-side fetches and out of scope. A thin app-level pre-check would still be worth adding alongside it for a categorized ADR-0009-style hint instead of a silent firewall-drop timeout, but is not the security boundary itself.

title: Typed missing-field report instead of prose 'not stated'
description: Audit (docs/findings/2026-08-07-a2web-call-trace-audit.md) §2/§3.2/§3.3: 423 calls (14%) admit a gap in prose ('not stated/not shown/not listed'); 120 are stock, 68 price, 37 product URLs. The caller cannot distinguish 'the page does not have it' from 'we failed to read it', so it re-queries the same unchanged URL with re-worded text — 60 observed. Samples show the caller coaching extraction strategy ('Read the JSON-LD/offers', then 'Find and state the exact numeric price in rubles'), and asking again for variant/size-selector stock never returned the first time. Proposal: per-field found/reason report (js_rendered | absent_on_page | extraction_failed) — the ADR-0015 withheld-body-index principle applied to fields. Envelope shape change: Ask First.

title: Surface the page's primary image URL so a multimodal caller can look at it
description: Today the `ask`/`query` envelope drops every image signal: `_ASK_META_ALLOWLIST` in src/a2web/fetcher_response.py:263 keeps only `og.description`, and `og.image*` is explicitly named as carrying 'zero incremental signal'. That judgement was made for a text-only caller. Most callers are now multimodal and can READ a product photo — spec sheet on the box, colour, size chart, a variant grid, a price sticker baked into the hero image — which is exactly the information a2web most often fails to extract as prose. Concrete case: product pages. When a2web answers a question about an item and CANNOT confirm the product details from prose (the ask that motivated this: 'if I didn't find that it is a product'), the answer is thin, but the page still has a hero image the caller could interpret itself. Handing back the image URL turns a thin answer into a usable one at no extraction cost. Not a new fetch, not an embed: emit the URL only, and only when it is grounded in the page (og:image / twitter:image / JSON-LD Product.image / the literal hero src) — ADR-0014 holds, no pattern-guessed CDN URLs. ADR-0012 also holds: relay the image the page itself designates as primary, never rank a gallery by a2web's own criterion.
design: Open questions to settle before implementing, not blockers for filing: 1. SCOPE — product pages only, or any page with a designated primary image? Denis framed it around products; the mechanism is generic. Leaning: generic emit, since 'is this a product' is itself an unreliable classification, and the value case is 'prose extraction came up short', which is not product-specific. 2. TRIGGER — always, or only when the answer is thin / low-confidence / the product was not confirmed? Always-on is simpler and testable; conditional risks another verdict-shaped decision spread across sites. 3. SHAPE — a typed field on the envelope (`primary_image`? part of an images list with a source label) vs re-admitting `og.image` to _ASK_META_ALLOWLIST. A typed field is preferable — the meta dict is untyped and the allowlist comment already says meta is for debug. Envelope-shape change => Ask First (AGENTS.md). 4. GROUNDING — precedence order across og:image / twitter:image / JSON-LD Product.image / hero , and what to do with a gallery (relay in source order, do not crown).
acceptance_criteria: A page carrying a designated primary image emits its URL on the ask/query envelope, sourced from page content (og:image, twitter:image, JSON-LD image, or a literal src) and never pattern-guessed. A page with no such image emits nothing rather than a placeholder. Tests: one captured product fixture asserting the URL is relayed, one asserting a page without an image stays silent, and one asserting the emitted URL appears verbatim in the source HTML (ADR-0014 grounding). Envelope-shape change is confirmed with Denis before it ships.

title: Redundant thin_content duplication when include_content=True on thin verdict
description: query()'s build_ask_response (src/a2web/fetcher_response.py:1002 and :1039) sets both thin_content and content_md from the identical fr.content_md string whenever a caller passes include_content=True on a fetch that terminates in a thin/empty-confirmed verdict. thin_content exists per ADR-0015 to force the body onto the wire when query withholds it by default (include_content=False) — but when the caller already opted into content_md, that forcing job is already done and thin_content becomes a byte-for-byte duplicate. Fix: omit thin_content whenever content_md is already non-empty on the wire (presence-guard pattern, same shape as existing wire.py encoder fixes) instead of unconditionally populating it whenever the content_thin hint or empty_confirmed fires. Need to check whether the empty_confirmed path deserves the same guard or has different stakes (it's the promoted-ok/never-cached case). Also needs ADR-0015 + openspec/specs/ask-response/spec.md updated to state the contract explicitly: callers check content_md first, thin_content is a fallback only when the body was withheld. No existing test covers include_content=True + thin outcome together (tests/capabilities/retrieval_completeness/test_thin_semantics.py only exercises include_content=False).
acceptance_criteria: thin_content is omitted from the AskResponse wire when content_md is already non-empty (include_content=True) for a thin or empty-confirmed outcome; existing include_content=False behavior unchanged; empty_confirmed path explicitly reviewed and handled (same guard or documented reason not to); ADR-0015 and openspec/specs/ask-response/spec.md updated to state content_md-first / thin_content-fallback contract; new test covers include_content=True + thin verdict; make check green.

title: confidence: high on a null answer that sat next to two browser failure hints
description:
Call #1 returned confidence='high' on the answer 'This page does not provide the current status ... for tracking number 7957139164' -- while the same envelope carried browser_internal_error AND browser_unavailable hints.

If the browser tier died, confidence in the negative claim 'the page does not have it' cannot be high: the page may well have had it behind the render that failed. A confident absence claim next to a failed retrieval is the ADR-0009 harm wearing a different hat -- the caller reads a miss as a complete answer.

UNCONFIRMED against current code -- verify how confidence is computed relative to failed-rung observations before implementing.
acceptance_criteria: A negative/absence answer cannot carry high confidence when a retrieval rung failed on that fetch; pinned by a test.
close_reason: Confirmed against current code: _confidence_for(verdict, content_md) only looks at final verdict + length, blind to whether a browser rung was dispatched and failed earlier in the same fetch. Added a downgrade-only cap in build_response (fetcher_response.py), same precedent as the existing served_url_differs cap: when operator_hints carries browser_internal_error or browser_unavailable, a computed high confidence is capped to medium (no new hint needed — the browser-failure hint already explains why). This is a general failed-rung cap, not negative-answer NLP detection (no cheap signal for 'this is an absence claim' exists at this layer) — it strictly covers the reported case since ALL answers including negative ones get capped when a browser rung failed. New fetch-response spec Requirement + 4 tests. Mutation-verified. make check + make recon-check green.

title: other_pages ships duplicate URLs across kinds, with 'discussed page' as a non-reason
description:
The DHL tracking query returned six other_pages rows over three distinct URLs: login.html and dhlexpresscommerce.com each appear once as kind=structural and again as kind=drilldown. The structural copies carry reason='discussed page' -- a non-reason that says nothing to the caller.

Two defects: (a) no dedup across kinds, so the caller pays wire cost twice for the same fetch; (b) a placeholder reason string shipping as if it were content.

Note the constraint from CLAUDE.md: a later stage may ADD to an index, never silently replace or relabel a producer's claim -- so dedup must MERGE (keep the more specific reason, decide a kind precedence deliberately), not drop one side arbitrarily.
acceptance_criteria: other_pages is deduped by URL with an explicit merge rule; 'discussed page' either carries real content or the row is omitted rather than shipping a placeholder.
close_reason: other_pages is now deduped by URL in _compose_other_pages (fetcher_response.py) via a new _dedupe_other_pages helper: the same URL surfaced independently by handler-continuation, LLM-structural, and LLM-drilldown producers now ships once, with an explicit merge rule rather than an arbitrary drop — a page-specific reason wins over a generic catalog-classifier placeholder (discussed page/item page/discussion thread), and a tie is broken by kind precedence (structural over drilldown). New ask-response spec Requirement + 4 unit tests including the exact reported DHL shape (login.html + commerce host each doubled across structural/drilldown). Mutation-verified. make check + make recon-check green.

title: nginx default welcome page classified as length_floor:thin_fallthrough, not as non-content
description:
fetch_raw of https://www.dhl.com/utapi?trackingNumber=...&language=en fell through to the ARCHIVE tier and returned the nginx default welcome page ('If you see this page, the nginx web server is successfully installed and working'), which a2web then classified length_floor:thin_fallthrough.

An nginx/Apache default page is a recognizable non-content fingerprint -- 'this is not the page you asked for' is a stronger and more honest verdict than 'thin'. Also worth asking why the archive tier served a default-vhost snapshot at all.

Related invariant: empty-vs-wall-discrimination -- this is a third category (wrong-page), and calling it thin understates it.

title: Two self-contradicting browser hints in one envelope
description:
The same envelope carried both:

  1. browser_internal_error -- 'Page.goto: net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR at <url>' (so the browser ran and navigated)
  2. browser_unavailable -- 'browser launch failed: could not find a valid browser binary ... (binary OK: Google Chrome for Testing 148.0.7778.96; failure is in the CDP handshake, not the binary)'

So the browser both ran and could not be found, and hint 2 contradicts its own parenthetical in the same sentence. title: published carries schema/copyright boilerplate dates (2018-01-01, 2000-01-01)
description:
Both DHL pages reported a published date: 2018-01-01 on dhl.com tracking, 2000-01-01 on gumruk.dhl.com.tr. These are almost certainly copyright-footer or schema-boilerplate dates, not publication dates.

A confidently wrong published is worse than an absent one -- an agent caller has no way to tell a real date from a footer artifact, and 2000-01-01 will silently mis-sort anything that ranks by recency.

UNCONFIRMED -- verify where published is sourced (JSON-LD? meta? footer scrape?) before deciding. Candidate fix: reject implausible sentinel dates (Jan-1 with no time, dates far older than the domain's content) rather than shipping them.
acceptance_criteria: Boilerplate/sentinel dates are dropped rather than shipped as published; a corpus entry covers a page whose only date is a copyright footer.
close_reason: Confirmed against current code: published is sourced from content_extract (shelf, trafilatura.extract_metadata) at the single chokepoint fc.published = extract_result.published (extract.py:141), never branched on elsewhere. Both reported dates (2018-01-01 dhl.com, 2000-01-01 gumruk.dhl.com.tr) are bare Jan-1 — trafilatura's date field carries no time component, so 'Jan-1 with no time' collapses to one testable fact (month=1, day=1), the recurring shape of a copyright-footer/schema-boilerplate artifact. Added _is_sentinel_date() and filtered at the extraction chokepoint (kept in a2web, not promoted into the shelf content_extract package — a targeted post-filter, not a shelf change). New extraction spec Requirement + 4 tests (2 unit on the predicate, 2 through the real _phase_extract with extract_markdown monkeypatched). Mutation-verified via Edit (not git checkout --). make check (1783 passed, 91.96% cov) + make recon-check (8 > floor 1) green.

title: Decide which failure-envelope fields are load-bearing for an agent caller vs debug noise
description:
A single thin-200 failure shipped status, tier, confidence, narrative, diagnostics_summary, retrieval_incomplete AND the hint -- restating one fact four ways:

  narrative:           'archive -> length_floor:thin_fallthrough (2.5s).'
  diagnostics_summary: 'tier=archive verdict=length_floor total_ms=2506 extras=thin_fallthrough'
  status: failed + retrieval_incomplete: true   (does one imply the other?)
  tier: archive                                  (deviation field -- useful to the caller?)

Question to settle, NOT a fix to apply blind: which of these an AGENT caller acts on, vs which is operator debug that belongs behind debug=True.

Weigh against ADR-0009: the floor is loud, explicit incompleteness -- trimming here must not quiet the miss signal. narrative and diagnostics_summary are already failure-only tiers in _prune_wire; the candidate question is whether diagnostics_summary should join the debug group.

Also folds in the sibling question from the same session: headings duplicating content_md. In the last fetch_raw, headings held a single entry verbatim equal to the first ## line of the attached body. When the body ships, headings may be pure duplication -- but headings is cheap and fetch_raw callers may index on it, so measure before cutting.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded (ADR or design note) naming which fields stay on the failure wire and which move behind debug, with the ADR-0009 argument addressed explicitly. Implementation is a follow-up bead.
